introduction: The durable job queue is an internal Go package (`internal/jobqueue/`) that provides SQLite-backed persistent background job execution for the af-hub, supporting retry with exponential backoff, per-key serialization, crash recovery, and graceful shutdown. It is a foundational building block with no REST API of its own — consumers register job type handlers and expose their own domain endpoints.

glossary.CancelJob: A queue method that transitions a queued job to cancelled status; returns ErrNotCancellable for jobs in other statuses.
glossary.CountByStatus: A queue method that returns a map of status string to integer count for all jobs of a given type.
glossary.ErrNotCancellable: A sentinel error returned by CancelJob when the target job is in a status that cannot be cancelled (running, completed, or dead_letter).
glossary.GetByID: A queue method that returns a single job record by its UUID identifier.
glossary.InitSchema: A Go function that creates the `jobs` table and its required indexes using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS statements.
glossary.ListByKey: A queue method that returns all job records for a specific type and key combination.
glossary.ListByType: A queue method that returns paginated job records filtered by type, with optional status and key filters.
glossary.ListOpts: A struct passed to ListByType that carries optional filter parameters (status, key) and pagination parameters (offset, limit).
glossary.WAL mode: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging journal mode (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL) required for concurrent readers and writers without serializing on the database lock.
glossary.WithWorkers: A functional option for the queue constructor that sets the number of worker goroutines.
glossary.available_at: An RFC 3339 timestamp column on a job record indicating the earliest time the job may be claimed by a worker; used to implement exponential backoff delays.
glossary.busy_timeout: A SQLite pragma (PRAGMA busy_timeout) that sets the maximum milliseconds to wait when the database is locked before returning SQLITE_BUSY.
glossary.crash recovery: The startup procedure that resets any jobs found in `running` status back to `queued` so they are re-dispatched after a hub restart or crash.
glossary.dead_letter: A terminal job status indicating the job has exhausted its retry limit or encountered a permanent error and will not be retried automatically.
glossary.grace period: The configurable maximum duration (default 30 seconds) the queue waits for in-flight handlers to complete during graceful shutdown before forcibly cancelling them.
glossary.idx_jobs_nonce: A unique SQLite index on the `nonce` column of the `jobs` table, used for fast nonce deduplication.
glossary.idx_jobs_status_available_at: A composite SQLite index on `status` and `available_at` columns, used by the polling query to find claimable queued jobs.
glossary.idx_jobs_type_created_at: A composite SQLite index on `type` and `created_at` columns, used for ListByType pagination ordered by creation time.
glossary.idx_jobs_type_key_status: A composite SQLite index on `type`, `key`, and `status` columns, used for duplicate-prevention and per-key serialization checks.
glossary.jobs: The SQLite table that persists all job records for the durable job queue.
glossary.nonce: A caller-supplied cryptographic string that uniquely identifies a specific job submission request, used to deduplicate retransmissions.
glossary.payload: A JSON blob stored on a job record containing job-type-specific input data; opaque to the queue itself.
glossary.poll interval: The configurable duration (default 5 seconds) a worker waits before re-polling for available jobs when no work is found and no wakeup signal arrives.
glossary.promote: The polling loop step that transitions `failed` jobs whose `available_at` has passed back to `queued` status.
glossary.result: A nullable JSON blob stored on a job record containing the handler's output on successful completion; opaque to the queue itself.
glossary.retry_count: An integer column on a job record tracking how many retry attempts have been made; incremented before each backoff delay is computed.
glossary.serialization key: The combination of `type` and `key` fields that determines which jobs must execute sequentially; at most one job with a given (type, key) pair may be in `running` status at any time.
glossary.stopCh: An internal Go channel closed by the queue during shutdown to broadcast a stop signal to all worker goroutines.
glossary.submitted_by: A string identifier on a job record indicating which user, agent, or system submitted the job.
glossary.wakeup channel: A buffered(1) Go channel shared by all worker goroutines; a non-blocking send on this channel wakes an idle worker when a new job is enqueued.
glossary.failed: A job status indicating the handler returned a retryable error. The job remains in this status with an updated available_at timestamp until the polling loop promotes it back to queued.

acceptance_criteria.action: creates a queue instance with default configuration (4 workers, 5s `poll interval`, 30s `grace period`) overridden by any provided options; does not start worker goroutines
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (*Queue, error); error is non-nil only if configuration is invalid
acceptance_criteria.trigger: New is called with a *sql.DB and zero or more functional options

acceptance_criteria.action: runs `crash recovery`, then starts the configured number of worker goroutines, then logs queue started at INFO level
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns error if crash recovery fails; nil on success
acceptance_criteria.trigger: Start is called on a constructed queue

acceptance_criteria.action: overrides the default worker count of 4 with the provided value n

edge_cases.action: rejects the invalid configuration
edge_cases.return_contract: New returns (nil, non-nil error) indicating worker count must be positive
edge_cases.error_condition: WithWorkers is called with n <= 0

edge_cases.action: returns an error without starting additional worker goroutines
edge_cases.return_contract: returns non-nil error indicating the queue is already started
edge_cases.error_condition: Start is called on a queue that is already running

edge_cases.action: rejects the nil database connection
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, non-nil error) indicating db must not be nil
edge_cases.error_condition: New is called with a nil *sql.DB

correctness_properties.title: At-most-one-active-per-key invariant
correctness_properties.for_any: job type T and key K
correctness_properties.invariant: at most one job with (type=T, key=K) is in queued or running status at any time; Enqueue and RequeueDeadLetter both enforce this check before inserting or requeuing

correctness_properties.title: Nonce uniqueness across all jobs
correctness_properties.invariant: at most one job record with nonce=N exists in the `jobs` table at any time; a second Enqueue with the same nonce returns the existing job without inserting a new record

correctness_properties.title: Per-key serial execution
correctness_properties.for_any: job type T and key K
correctness_properties.invariant: at most one job with (type=T, key=K) is in running status at any time; the polling query's exclusion of keys with a running job enforces this even under concurrent workers

correctness_properties.title: Retry count monotonically increases until dead-letter
correctness_properties.for_any: job J that receives retryable errors
correctness_properties.invariant: retry_count is incremented exactly once per retryable failure; when retry_count exceeds max_retries the job transitions to dead_letter and retry_count is never incremented again

correctness_properties.title: Backoff delay is non-decreasing and capped
correctness_properties.for_any: retry_count values r1 < r2 for the same retry policy
correctness_properties.invariant: computed delay at r1 <= computed delay at r2 <= cap; no computed delay exceeds the configured cap value

correctness_properties.title: Crash recovery resets all running jobs
correctness_properties.invariant: after Start completes, no job remains in running status; all jobs that were running before the restart are in queued status with available_at <= now()

correctness_properties.title: Completed and dead-lettered jobs are terminal
correctness_properties.for_any: job J in completed or dead_letter status
correctness_properties.invariant: no worker transitions J out of completed or dead_letter status automatically; only an explicit RequeueDeadLetter call can move a dead_letter job back to queued

correctness_properties.title: Worker count matches configuration
correctness_properties.for_any: queue instance Q constructed with WithWorkers(n)
correctness_properties.invariant: after Start is called, exactly n worker goroutines are running; no more and no fewer goroutines are spawned

correctness_properties.title: Graceful shutdown completes within grace period
correctness_properties.for_any: shutdown event with grace period G
correctness_properties.invariant: Wait() returns within G seconds of Shutdown being called; if handlers are still running at G, their contexts are cancelled and Wait() returns regardless

correctness_properties.title: InitSchema is idempotent
correctness_properties.for_any: number of times InitSchema is called on the same database
correctness_properties.invariant: calling InitSchema multiple times produces the same schema as calling it once; no error is returned on subsequent calls

execution_paths.title: Happy-path job enqueue and successful execution

steps.action: calls Enqueue with type='merge', key='main', nonce='abc123', payload=JSON blob, submitted_by='user-1'
validates type is registered, checks nonce uniqueness, checks no active (type, key) job exists, inserts job record with status=queued and available_at=now()
performs non-blocking send on the `wakeup channel`
receives wakeup signal, runs promote step (no failed jobs to promote), polls for oldest claimable queued job
atomically claims the job by updating status to running with WHERE status='queued'
calls the registered merge handler with the job's `payload` and a context
executes the merge operation and returns (result, false, nil)
serializes result to JSON, updates job record with status=completed and result column, logs at DEBUG level
calls GetByID with the job ID and reads the completed job record including the `result` field

execution_paths.title: Retryable failure with exponential backoff and eventual success

steps.action: calls Enqueue with type='sync', key='repo-42', nonce='xyz789'
inserts job record with status=queued
claims the job, calls the sync handler
returns (nil, true, error('network timeout'))
increments retry_count to 1, computes delay=4s, sets status=failed, available_at=now()+4s
on next poll cycle, promote step finds the failed job with elapsed available_at and transitions it back to queued
claims the promoted queued job and calls the sync handler again
returns (result, false, nil) on the second attempt
updates job record with status=completed and stores result

execution_paths.title: Job exhausts retries and is dead-lettered

steps.action: calls Enqueue with a job type configured with max_retries=2
inserts job record with status=queued, retry_count=0
claims and executes the job; handler returns retryable error; retry_count incremented to 1, status=failed
promote step transitions job back to queued after backoff; worker claims and executes again; handler returns retryable error; retry_count incremented to 2, status=failed
promote step transitions job back to queued; worker claims and executes again; handler returns retryable error; retry_count incremented to 3 which exceeds max_retries=2
transitions job to dead_letter status, stores error message, logs at WARN level
calls ListByType with status filter=dead_letter to inspect the failed job
calls RequeueDeadLetter with the job ID after fixing the underlying issue
resets retry_count to 0, sets status=queued, available_at=now(), sends wakeup signal
claims job J1 and begins executing the handler
crashes or is killed before the handler completes; job J1 remains in running status in the `jobs` table
restarts and calls InitSchema (no-op since table exists), then calls Start on the queue
runs crash recovery: queries for jobs in running status, finds J1, resets it to queued with available_at=now(), logs at WARN level with job_id=J1
starts, polls, claims J1, and re-executes the handler (handler must be idempotent)
handler completes successfully; job transitions to completed
claims job J2 and begins executing a long-running handler
receives shutdown signal and calls Shutdown on the queue
closes `stopCh` to broadcast stop signal; worker loops stop claiming new jobs
waits up to the `grace period` (30s) for all workers to exit
handler completes within the grace period; worker finalizes the job and exits
Wait() returns; logs queue stopped at INFO level; hub process exits cleanly

execution_paths.title: Duplicate enqueue prevention for same (type, key)

steps.action: calls Enqueue with type='merge', key='feature-branch', nonce='n1'; job J3 is created with status=queued
calls Enqueue again with type='merge', key='feature-branch', nonce='n2' (different nonce, same type+key)
nonce 'n2' is unique so nonce check passes; duplicate-prevention check finds J3 is active (queued)
returns J3's ID with duplicate=true without inserting a new record
receives (J3_id, true, nil) and waits for J3 to complete before retrying

error_handling.condition: Enqueue called with an unregistered job type
error_handling.behavior: returns ("", false, non-nil error) without inserting any record

error_handling.condition: Enqueue called with an empty nonce
error_handling.behavior: returns ("", false, non-nil error) indicating nonce must not be empty

error_handling.condition: Register called with a duplicate type name
error_handling.behavior: returns non-nil error immediately (fail fast) without overwriting the existing handler

error_handling.condition: CancelJob called on a job in running, completed, or dead_letter status
error_handling.behavior: returns ErrNotCancellable without modifying the job record

error_handling.condition: CancelJob called with a non-existent job ID
error_handling.behavior: returns non-nil error with a not-found message

error_handling.condition: RequeueDeadLetter called when an active (queued or running) job exists for the same (type, key)
error_handling.behavior: returns (existingActiveJobID, non-nil error) indicating a duplicate active job exists

error_handling.condition: RequeueDeadLetter called for a job not in dead_letter status
error_handling.behavior: returns ("", non-nil error) indicating the job is not in dead_letter status

error_handling.condition: GetByID called with a non-existent job UUID
error_handling.behavior: returns (nil, non-nil error) with a not-found message
worker recovers from the panic, transitions the job to dead_letter with the panic message as the error, and continues processing other jobs

error_handling.condition: grace period expires before all in-flight handlers complete
error_handling.behavior: queue cancels in-flight handler contexts, logs one WARN line per interrupted job including job_id, and exits; interrupted jobs are reset to queued by crash recovery on next startup

error_handling.condition: crash recovery database query fails on startup
error_handling.behavior: Start returns non-nil error; no worker goroutines are started
New returns (nil, non-nil error) indicating worker count must be positive

error_handling.condition: job type found in database during polling has no registered handler
error_handling.behavior: worker transitions the job to dead_letter with an error message indicating no handler is registered; logs at WARN level

error_handling.condition: retry_count overflows or computed backoff delay overflows before cap is applied
error_handling.behavior: delay is clamped to the cap value without panicking or producing a negative delay

symbols.name: DB.ExecContext
